# Sanguine export

This file was made by Sanguine on your request. It is useful without the app.

## Files

- `events.jsonl`: the full log, one JSON object per line, oldest first. This is the source of truth. Sanguine can read it back (Settings > Privacy and data > Import). Each line has: `id`, `lamport` (order), `device_id`, `recorded_at` (when you logged it), `effective_day` (the day it is about), `tz`, `kind`, `payload`, `provenance` (manual, imported or sensor), `source_app`, `external_id`, `retracts` (set when a line undoes an earlier one) and `schema_v`.
- `cycles.csv`: one row per cycle. `start_day` is the first day of bleeding. `length_days` is the days until the next period started. `quality` is typical, or the reason a cycle is left out of estimates. `ovulation_*` columns are set only when a test or measurement dated it.
- `daily.csv`: one row per logged day: `flow` (none, spotting, light, medium, heavy), `flow_kind`, `clots`, `symptoms` (code:intensity from 1 to 3, separated by semicolons), `condom_used` and `has_note`. Notes are not exported in readable form.
- `biomarkers.csv`: temperature, ovulation test, cervical mucus and cervical position records. `value` is JSON.
- `manifest.json`: format name, version and counts.

## Notes

All dates are local calendar days (YYYY-MM-DD). Lines that undo an earlier line are kept in `events.jsonl` so nothing is lost; the CSV files show the result after those undos.

Sanguine estimates are ranges, not promises. Sanguine does not diagnose, screen for or treat any condition.
